name: PE700

name: Specifications
description: "Vacuum tube pre-main amplifier using P.A. T circuit.Valve300 uses 6L6, a high-sensitivity beam tube, in a push-pull manner.Although it was difficult to reproduce the natural beauty of music by simply operating the beam pentode in push-pull mode, the P.A. T circuit at Tokyo Sound achieves both power and the natural beauty of a single.P.A. T (Positive Alternating Turn) circuit is mounted in order to improve the weak point of the pentode (beam pentode).Conventional amplifiers employ methods such as triode connection, ultra-linear connection, or cathode feedback in order to improve the weak points of the pentode. The P.A. T. circuit employed in the Valve300 is a different method from those of the conventional ones. It improves the weak points of the pentode push-pull (ambiguity and opacity of sound, roughness of high-frequency range, etc.). In addition, the P.A. T. circuit operates like a triode by reducing the internal resistance of the vacuum tube, and increases the push-out feeling and elasticity feeling of low-frequency range.Refer to the figure below for an overview of the P.A. T. circuit.Pentode (or beam pentode) DC voltage of + B2 is supplied to SG of V1/V2 through resistor AA' in direct current, while AC signal is supplied from P1 of OPT through resistor B' to SG of V2, from P2 through resistor B to SG of V1, and from P2 through resistor B to SG of V1. Capacitor C/C' is added in parallel to resistor A/A'.The SG of V1/V2 receives a slight positive feedback from the counter electrode P via B, and is in phase with CG. This is like a combination of CG and SG in terms of AC. Although the output decreases slightly, the internal resistance of the sphere decreases, so it becomes a triode operating state. In addition, by adding CC' to AA', the middle and high range becomes smooth and the low sound becomes rich. By supplying power to SG from + b2 through AA' resistance, SG is fixed DC and this function is established.
